question_stem:
You may not need to use all of the materials provided.
1
In this experiment, you will investigate a light-dependent resistor (LDR).
question_stem_latex:
You may not need to use all of the materials provided.
1
In this experiment, you will investigate a light-dependent resistor (LDR).

parts.label: (a)
parts.question_text:
•
Connect the circuit shown in Fig. 1.1.
•
Ensure that the switch S is open.
•
Slide the LDR leads into the tube until the front of the LDR is just level with the open end
of the tube, as shown in Fig. 1.1.
•
With the LDR in this position, attach a piece of adhesive tape to the leads as a marker at
the other end of the tube, as shown in Fig. 1.1.
•
Slide the tube until the LDR is approximately half-way along it, as shown in Fig. 1.2.
•
The distance between the tape and the tube is x.
Measure and record x.
•
Close S and record the ammeter reading I.
•
Open S.

parts.label: (b)
parts.question_text:
Change x by moving the LDR to a new position inside the tube, with x in the range 4 cm to
18 cm. Record x and I.
Repeat until you have six sets of values of x and I.
Record your results in a table. Include values of I in your table.

parts.question_text: Plot a graph of I on the y-axis against x on the x-axis.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.question_text: Draw the straight line of best fit.
parts.question_text_latex: Draw the straight line of best fit.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.question_text: Determine the gradient and y-intercept of this line.
parts.question_text_latex: Determine the gradient and y-intercept of this line.

parts.label: (d)
parts.question_text:
It is suggested that the quantities I and x are related by the equation
I = ax + b
where a and b are constants.
Using your answers in (c)(iii), determine the values of a and b.
Give appropriate units.
